title: auth-quota-hypothesis-sketchbook
content:
Goal: quick brain dump of recent 401/429 signals from customers A/B and a set of commands/observations to repro and validate hypotheses. This is messy — notes to self + next steps.

Context / short timeline:
- Mar 1: Customer A reported intermittent 429s from their background workers between 03:10-04:30 UTC. Mostly during load spike (burst writes). They use two API keys (app and worker) under same org. No config changes on their side.
- Mar 3: Customer B observed auth failures (401) when rotating ephemeral keys via their internal vault. They use short-lived JWTs exchanged for API keys via /v1/auth/exchange.
- Mar 5: We saw a small uptick in 429s originating from the ap-southeast-1 region; correlation with burst autoscaling activity on dedicated pools.

Quick reproduction commands I ran locally (replace <KEY> / <HOST> / <TOKEN>):
- Simple generation request (curl):
  curl -s -D - \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hi"}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

- If I want to capture response headers to inspect rate-limit info:
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"small","input":"x"}'

- Token exchange flow that Customer B uses (repro):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/auth/exchange -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"jwt":"<SHORT_LIVED_JWT>"}'

Observed error snippets (real logs anonymized):
- 429 payloads (JSON):
  {"error":"Too many requests", "code":"rate_limit_exceeded", "details":"burst cap reached for api-key"}
- 401 payloads (JSON):
  {"error":"Unauthorized", "code":"invalid_token", "details":"token expired or signature mismatch"}

Sample response headers we've observed in-prod (from syslogs):
- x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 240
- x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1677629400
- x-rw-organization-id: org_03aC
- Via: 1.1 varnish

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
1) Aggregated quota bleed between multiple API keys under same org — customers think they have headroom per key but quota is org-level for some endpoints. Evidence: 429s show "burst cap reached for api-key" but header x-rw-organization-id present and traffic from two keys spikes at same time.
2) Token exchange race: ephemeral JWTs not fully propagated to caching layer (edge) causing transient 401s when vault rotates and clients reuse cached token -> auth service rejects due to small clock skew or TTL misinterpretation.
3) Autoscaler churn: when dedicated pool scales quickly, proxy routing causes double-counting of inflight tokens in our per-route sliding-window implementation, leading to temporary over-limit detection.
4) Client-side retry behavior not honoring Retry-After header, causing thundering herd against the same quota window (amplifies 429s). Logs show some clients retrying every 1s.
5) Header normalization bug: proxies strip x-rw-headers on certain paths causing our quota middleware to miss grouping keys correctly.

Tests to run (ordered):
- Verify org-level vs key-level quota mapping:
  * Run two concurrent clients using two different keys under same org hitting /v1/generate at controlled RPS and observe x-rw-rate-limit-remaining. Script idea:
    for i in 1..200; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY1" ... & curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY2" ... ; sleep 0.1; done
  * Capture metrics from quota service around that time (time series: quota.used_by_org, quota.used_by_key).

- Reproduce the token-exchange 401:
  * Use a test JWT with TTL 5s, exchange for key, sleep 4s, call generate -> expect success; repeat with slight clock shift on client (+3s) to see failure.
  * Use curl with explicit Date header to simulate client clock skew: curl -H "Date: $(date -u -d '+3 seconds' --rfc-2822)" ...

- Edge cache propagation test:
  * Exchange token, hit edge in region A and region B, then rotate token and immediately hit both edges to see if propagation delay causes 401s in one region only.

- Autoscale churn test:
  * Simulate burst that triggers dedicated pool scaling: create load that ramps 10x in 30s and measure whether per-route inflight counters spike unexpectedly.

Quick notes from config / logs I checked:
- Quota service config for /v1/generate shows "scope": ["org", "api_key"] and default window 60s, burst_cap 300. But enforcement appears to check org bucket first, then key bucket.
- Edge cache (VCL) has a 1s cache for auth exchange responses (intended), but logs show a few cache-miss spikes when upstream auth latency > 200ms.
- Observed a pattern where x-rw-rate-limit-reset epoch sometimes in the future by >60s during autoscale events — suggests clock skew in some quota nodes.

Example CLI reproduction I ran and paste of raw response (sanitized):
- Repro run: two parallel invocations at t0 with two keys -> one returned 200, the other 429 with headers:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 04:12:50 GMT
  x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1710298370
  Retry-After: 30
  Content-Type: application/json

  {"error":"Too many requests","code":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":30}

Notes / oddities to investigate with infra+quota owners:
- Confirm whether org-level quota uses strict or leaky-bucket semantics. If strict counters it will more easily cause hard 429s on bursts.
- Check for any recent change to edge caching of auth responses over last 2 weeks (PRs around auth-cache TTL). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2142
- Validate clock sync between quota nodes and edge proxies (ntp/chrony drift). We saw reset times out by ~90s in a few samples.
- Audit retry middleware in customers' SDKs: look for exponential backoff and honoring Retry-After. Initiate outreach with CS to ask 3rd-party SDKs logging retry patterns.

Immediate next steps (me):
- Run the org-vs-key concurrent script and collect quota metrics. (planned Mar 13 window 02:00-03:00 UTC)
- Open a small test deploy that uses a 5s TTL JWT to validate exchange path edge propagation. Assign to Omar to help.
- Ask infra to run a clock-drift check on quota nodes in ap-southeast-1 and us-west-2.
- Draft a short CC message to Customer A explaining initial findings and asking if they can temporarily limit background worker concurrency while we test.

TODO/TODOs:
- [ ] Add more reproducible scripts into repo under tests/ratelimit
- [ ] If hypothesis #1 confirmed, propose per-key soft quota with per-org hard cap as a mitigation
- [ ] Add more verbose logging in auth-exchange path for cache hits/misses (dev-only flag)

Questions for on-call:
- Is it safe to temporarily bump org-level quota for a customer to reduce production impact while we investigate? (pros/cons?)
- Do we have limits on how many keys an org can create that might cause unexpected aggregation? If not, consider limit.

Misc scratch items:
- Observed client that sets Accept-Encoding: gzip and sends compressed payloads; edge sometimes returns 401 when payload is gzipped (possible proxy anomaly). Need to capture exact req/resp pair.
- Note to self: when capturing headers with curl -i sometimes Varnish adds Via header that confuses matching scripts; prefer -D headers.txt approach.

End of brain dump. Will tidy later and promote to eng ticket once repro script produces consistent signals.
